title: Decompose aggregate changes into segment-level contributions
when_to_use: When analyzing a drop or rise in an aggregate metric (e.g., department conversion rate) over time
experience:
- Calculate the metric for each sub-segment (e.g., role, team) in the baseline and comparison periods
- Compute each segment's contribution to the overall change using weighted averages (segment proportion * segment change)
- Rank segments by absolute contribution to identify the largest drivers
- Validate that segment proportions (mix) are stable; if not, separate mix effect from rate effect
- Report top segments causing the decline/increase with their contribution magnitude
checklist: Identify all relevant sub-segments in the data
Calculate period-over-period metric for each segment
Compute segment's weight in total population
common_failure_prevented: Missing which specific roles drove the Engineering department's conversion rate drop (e.g., not quantifying Frontend vs. Backend contributions)

title: Control for confounding factors when comparing manager performance
when_to_use: When evaluating individual performance metrics (e.g., conversion rates) across different managers or teams
experience:
- Identify potential confounders: job types/roles, experience levels, time periods, or resource differences
- Use regression with fixed effects (e.g., manager dummy variables + role controls) to isolate manager impact
- Calculate residuals (actual - predicted) for each manager after controlling for confounders
- Rank managers by residuals to identify systematic over/under-performance
- Check for interaction effects (e.g., does manager performance vary by role type?)
checklist: List all non-manager factors that could affect the metric
Test for manager*role interactions if relevant
Report managers with significantly low/high adjusted performance
common_failure_prevented: Concluding a manager has low performance without adjusting for the different roles/conditions they handle

title: Quantify intensity changes when analyzing process metrics
when_to_use: When analyzing conversion rates in a multi-stage process (e.g., application → interview → hire)
experience:
- Map the process stages and identify intensity metrics (e.g., interviews per application, time between stages)
- Calculate intensity for each period and segment (e.g., quarterly, by role)
- Test correlation between intensity changes and conversion rate changes
- Use regression to quantify impact: conversion_rate ~ intensity + controls
- Report whether changes in intensity explain the conversion rate drop
checklist: Define process stages and intermediate metrics
Plot intensity vs. conversion rate over time
Build regression model with intensity as predictor
common_failure_prevented: Not measuring whether the drop in conversion rate is due to fewer interviews per application or other process changes
